title: The Blue Parody band and its members
summary: Blue Parody was a nine-piece dance band, slightly less busy than Streeman; he names Angelo, the Quaglinas, S.J. Coogan and describes the instrumentation.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: You know, I never have known much about the Blue Parody except those brothers.

Well, they had a nine piece dance band and they had a good group. It was a good group, but Stremend had just a little better group. They played with a little more drive and of course they were getting three times more work than the Blue Parody. But the Blue Parody had a good group. They got work, but they didn't get as much as Stremend.
Who was in the Blue Parody?

Oh, I can't remember all the fellas. Well, Angelo was on trumpet. He was the band leader. A fellow on drums was a CPA nowadays. Phillip Quaglina was on trombone. Joe Quaglina was on third alto or first alto. I don't recall which one. A boy by the name of S.J. Coogan who worked for the federal government many years later. He was on saxophone, probably tenor sax I guess. Maybe he played lead alto. S.J. Coogan played lead alto. Joe Quaglina probably played lead a third, I don't recall which. And I can't remember. Johnny somebody was on drums. That's the guy that was a CPA later in the years. And I was on guitar, I wasn't on bass and I was still on six string guitar. I can't recall, I can't remember who was on piano. That's too far back.
Yeah, and you had, did he have one or two trumpets? What did they have?

Well if it was an eight piece band he had one trumpet and he had one trombone. If you had a nine piece band they would add another trumpet. You would have two trumpets and a trombone. So it really depended on the work, on the engagement. If you had a nine piece booking you would have three brass. You would have first trumpet, second trumpet and trombone. And you would add a second trumpet.
And who was the bass horn player that you were playing? Did we get his name or do you?
I can't remember who was on bass with Blue Parity because I was only with that group four months. What kind of a? But they had a good group, it was a good band. What did they get?
Did they get spots or sticks? You know I was fortunate.
Every band I ever played with was a good band. I can't put any band down. I was very fortunate.
